profile.name: Alicia Moreno
profile.main_concern:
I have three specialists for three different problems: a rash, something in my urine and low blood counts. Each one says to wait and recheck. I keep feeling worse and my joints hurt.

Symptoms: Joint pain and stiffness in hands and wrists (about 4 months): Stiff for about 45 minutes in the morning.; Facial rash after sun (about 3 months): Across cheeks and nose.; Fatigue (about 4 months); Mouth sores (on and off for 2 months): Painless, on the roof of my mouth.; Hair thinning (about 3 months); Fingers turn white or blue in the cold (last winter); Low-grade fevers (a few times since August): Around 37.8 C.; Ankle puffiness in the evening (about 1 month)

My questions: Could my rash, kidney results and blood counts be related? Is there a test I should ask about? Is it OK to keep taking naproxen?

summary.plain_language_summary: Alicia, the records show several findings that deserve a coordinated review rather than being followed only as separate skin, kidney, and blood issues. Your skin biopsy is not specific to one condition, and the urine test shows blood and protein, including red-cell casts, while kidney filtration was preserved at the time of testing. The blood count also showed low levels in several blood-cell types. Together with the reported joint stiffness, sun-related rash, mouth sore, and other symptoms, these findings make it reasonable to ask your doctors whether shared evaluation and additional blood tests are appropriate; the records do not establish a common cause. Please clarify soon what kidney tests and follow-up are scheduled, and whether the blood-count recheck should happen earlier than planned. Also confirm whether you are taking lisinopril and discuss naproxen with its prescriber in view of the kidney findings.

key_findings.text: Urine testing showed blood and protein, misshapen red cells, and red-cell casts; the urine protein/creatinine ratio was above the report's reference.
Kidney filtration was preserved in the recorded test, with creatinine 0.9 mg/dL and eGFR above 90.
The CBC showed low white cells, lymphocytes, hemoglobin, and platelets; the smear reported no blasts or schistocytes.
The facial rash worsens with sun exposure, and the skin biopsy shows a pattern that can occur in more than one condition and needs clinical and blood-test correlation.
The dermatology note also records hair thinning and a painless mouth ulcer.
The hematology note recommends repeating the CBC in three months; ask whether that timing still fits the current symptoms and findings.

connections.text: Ask whether the skin biopsy and rash, urine abnormalities, low blood counts, and reported joint symptoms should be reviewed together. The records do not establish that they share a cause.
Preserved kidney filtration is reassuring context, but it does not remove the need to follow up the abnormal urine findings and the planned repeat tests.

The plan to recheck the blood count in three months may need review in light of the low counts and the symptoms and urine findings; ask hematology or primary care whether the timing or evaluation should change.
Discuss naproxen with its prescriber and nephrology alongside the urine findings and the lisinopril plan. Confirm whether lisinopril was started and is currently being taken.

Vacuolar interface change along the dermal-epidermal junction with
